extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, agents, and IP practitioners filing or prosecuting appeals, utility models, and industrial designs before the IPOPHL
extracted.subtask_short: filing utility model and industrial design
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and formal requirements for filing, prosecuting, appealing, publishing, and obtaining registration for utility models and industrial designs (and related appeal procedures) under the IPOPHL Regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to Director for non-appealable Examiner actions (Rule 1301)
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions may be filed with the Director from any repeated action or requirement of the Examiner which is not subject to appeal and in other appropriate circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition must comply with prescribed time and manner; briefs or memoranda should accompany or be embodied in the petition. Director may direct Examiner to furnish a written statement (Examiner's Brief) setting forth reasons. Filing a petition does not stay the 4-month period for replying to Examiner actions nor other proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal to the Director (Rule 1302)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant may appeal to the Director upon final refusal of the Examiner or from any adverse action within the Examiner's original jurisdiction; a second adverse decision on same grounds may be considered final for appeal purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeal must comply with prescribed time and manner in the Regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director inhibition for conflict of interest (Rule 1302.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: After preliminary review, the Director may inhibit from deciding an appeal or petition if there is a conflict of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director must issue a Resolution stating reasons for inhibition and direct the Assistant Director to render a decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of unappealed final Examiner decision (Rule 1303)
rubrics_metrics.description: A final Examiner decision not appealed within the permitted time (or not prosecuted if appealed) is final and has res judicata effect on the same subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order declaring an application withdrawn for failure to respond or failure to file petition for revival likewise has res judicata effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time and manner for petitions and appeals (Rule 1304)
rubrics_metrics.description: Petition or notice of appeal must be filed in duplicate within a non-extendible period of two (2) months from the mailing date of the action subject to the petition or appeal, with full payment of required fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition/appeal must specify facts, points to be reviewed, grounds, and be signed and verified by petitioner/appellant or attorney of record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appellant's Brief filing requirement (Rule 1305)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon appeal, the appellant shall file an Appellant's Brief within a non-extendible period of thirty (30) days from the date of filing the notice of appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Brief must contain authorities and arguments relied upon; appeal dismissed for failure to file within time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner's Answer / Examiner's Brief (Rule 1306)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner shall submit to the Director an Examiner's brief containing a written statement in answer to the petition or appellant's brief within thirty (30) days from issuance of an order directing such statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copy must be served on petitioner or appellant by the Examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appellant's Reply limited to new points (Rule 1307)
rubrics_metrics.description: Appellant may file a reply brief directed only to new points raised in the Examiner's answer within a non-extendible thirty (30) day period from receipt of the Examiner's answer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director decision and appeal to Director General (Rule 1308)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director's decision reversing Examiner refusal is immediately final and executory; if Director affirms refusal, applicant may file notice of appeal to the Director General within one (1) month from receipt of Director's decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No motion for reconsideration of Director's decision allowed. Upon Director's decision becoming final, the application is remanded to the Examiner. Office of Director General may grant a single 15-day extension upon proper motion and payment before expiration of reglementary period; no further extensions. IPOPHL Memorandum Circular No. 2020-041 (Revised Uniform Rules on Appeal) applies suppletorily.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appellant's Brief to Director General (Rule 1309)
rubrics_metrics.description: Appellant shall file a brief within a non-extendible thirty (30) days from filing notice of appeal to the Director General containing authorities and arguments to maintain the appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeal dismissed for failure to file brief within time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director's Comment to Director General (Rule 1310)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director shall submit comments on the appellant's brief to the Director General within thirty (30) days if required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal to Court of Appeals and finality (Rule 1311)
rubrics_metrics.description: Decision of Director General reversing Director is immediately final and executory; if Director General affirms Director's refusal, applicant must perfect appeal to Court of Appeals per Rules of Court or refusal becomes final and executory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No motion for reconsideration of Director General's decision allowed. When Director's decision becomes final and executory, application remanded to Examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registrable utility model standard (Rule 1400)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any technical solution of a problem in any field of human activity which is new and industrially applicable shall be registrable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-registrable utility models (Rule 1401)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisions regarding 'Non-Patentable Inventions' in Part 2, Rule 202 of the Patent Regulations apply, mutatis mutandis, to non-registrable utility models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-reference to non-patentable categories (e.g., discoveries, scientific theories) as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial applicability definition (Rule 1402)
rubrics_metrics.description: A utility model which can be produced and used in any industry shall be industrially applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility model application channels and language (Rule 1403)
rubrics_metrics.description: Utility model application must be in writing, in Filipino or English, and filed through IPOPHL electronic filing system, electronic format/internet (if available), or IPSOs; addressed to the Director. Filing only via enumerated means.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application must include specified contents (see separate criterion for contents).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of utility model application (Rule 1403 list)
rubrics_metrics.description: The application shall contain: (a) request for registration; (b) description (title, technical field, background, summary, brief description of drawings, detailed description); (c) claims; (d) drawings if necessary; (e) abstract; (f) payment of required fees at filing; (g) appointment of agent/representative if applicant not a Philippine resident.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All listed elements are required for a proper filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title requirements for utility model (Rule 1403.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Title should be short, specific, in technical terms referring to technical features; no fancy names, brand names, or trademarks; appears as heading on first page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical field statement (Rule 1403.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement of the technical field of the art to which the utility pertains directed to the subject matter of the claimed utility model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Background of the utility model (Rule 1403.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide description of background art including state of the art, related arts, known technology relevant to the utility model; include references to specific documents and sources where possible and explain the technical problem the utility model intends to solve thoroughly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be as specific as possible; cite documents and sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary of the utility model (Rule 1403.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Summary must disclose the utility model as claimed, explaining the technical problem and its technical solution, and state differences versus background art in terms of advantages and benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brief description of drawings (Rule 1403.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every view of the drawings should be briefly described and given figure numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed description requirements (Rule 1403.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed description must completely specify the manner of making and using the utility model to enable a person of ordinary skill in the art to understand and practice it; set forth the precise and exact utility model as claimed; distinguish it from relevant prior art; and indicate the technical problem solved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisions for detailed description in Part 4 Rules 405-409 of Patent Regulations apply mutatis mutandis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract requirements and length (Rule 1403.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstract must be on a separate sheet with heading and title, consist of a concise summary of disclosure contained in description, claims, and drawings preferably not more than 150 words, drafted to clearly convey technical problem, gist of solution, and principal use(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstract serves merely as technical information; preferably disclose scope to serve as efficient search basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Working model requirement reference (Rule 1403.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisions regarding working models in Part 4 Rules 420-420.5 of Patent Regulations apply mutatis mutandis to utility model applications when required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim drafting requirements (Rule 1403.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims must define the subject matter sought, be clear and concise, and fully supported by the description. For improvements, claims should specifically point out and distinctly claim the improvement with a preamble indicating necessary prior art features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claim requirements in Part 4 Rules 416(a),(c),(d),(e) and 417 apply mutatis mutandis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation of application documents (Rule 1403.10(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Description, claims, and abstract may contain chemical or mathematical formulas; description and abstract may contain tables. Claims may contain tables only if subject matter makes tables desirable. Tables/formulas may be placed sideways if necessary with tops to left side.

rubrics_metrics.name: Units, symbols, and terminology (Rule 1403.10(b)-(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Physical values expressed in internationally recognized units (metric/SI) where appropriate; data not meeting requirement must also be expressed in recognized units. Use symbols in general use for mathematics and chemistry; use technical terms, signs, symbols generally accepted in the field. Terminology and signs must be consistent throughout application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment of fees upon filing (Rule 1404)
rubrics_metrics.description: Utility model application subject to full payment of filing fee and publication fees upon filing. Applications claiming priority at filing must pay priority claim fee with filing and publication fee. Priority claimed within two months subject to priority claim fee upon filing such claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of non-payment of fees (Rule 1404.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to pay all required fees in full upon filing means application will not be considered bona fide and is deemed a failed application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may retrieve failed application by formal written request within four (4) months from mailing date of notice of failed application. Failed application not retrieved is expunged. Failed due to non-payment not published and may be filed anew.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims incurring fee applies (Rule 1405)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provision on 'Claims incurring Fee' in Part 4 Rule 418 of Patent Regulations applies mutatis mutandis to utility models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date requisites for utility model (Rule 1406)
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing date is the date Office received these elements in English or Filipino: (a) request indicating utility model registration; (b) abstract; (c) description; (d) at least one claim; (e) drawings if necessary; (f) payment of required fees at filing; (g) appointment of agent if applicant not Philippines resident.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incomplete application rules apply (Rule 1406.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisions on 'Incomplete Applications' in Part 6 Rules 600.1 and 600.2 of Patent Regulations apply mutatis mutandis to incomplete utility model applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: According a filing date rules apply (Rule 1406.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provision on 'According a Filing Date to Applications' in Part 6 Rule 601 applies mutatis mutandis to utility models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Late-filed or missing drawings rules apply (Rule 1406.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provision on 'Late-filed or Missing Drawings' in Part 6 Rule 603 of Patent Regulations applies mutatis mutandis to utility model applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration process and registrability report (Rule 1407)
rubrics_metrics.description: Office shall adopt expeditious registration process. Applications registered without substantive examination if required fees and formal requirements complied with unless Director issues registrability report motu proprio. Director decides registration; may issue report and deny registration if prior art defeats registrability or direct applicant to amend and republish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may request a registrability report before enforcing rights to benefit from Office determination of novelty and industrial applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formality examination of utility model (Rule 1408)
rubrics_metrics.description: Office conducts formality examination and transmits report to applicant. Evaluation considers formality requirements including: non-registrable status; contents of request; priority documents; proof of authority; deed of assignment; payment of fees; signatures; identification of makers; contents of description/claims/abstract; formal drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report lists deficiencies; applicant must act within prescribed time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of utility model (Rule 1409)
rubrics_metrics.description: Only one independent genus or generic claim permissible in a utility model application; specific variations may be claimed in a reasonable number of dependent claims provided they fall under a single statutory class and single general innovative concept and within scope of generic claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction/division and entitlement of divisional (Rule 1410)
rubrics_metrics.description: Restriction or division of multiple embodiments proper if embodiments are independent and distinct or not specific variations; divisional filed during pendency is entitled to benefit of parent's filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisions for restriction in Part 6 Rules 604,606,607,608,610,611 apply mutatis mutandis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Term of divisional application (Rule 1410.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Term of a divisional application shall be seven (7) years from the date of filing of the parent application with no possibility of renewal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication timing and immediate publication conditions (Rule 1411)
rubrics_metrics.description: Utility model application published in IPOPHL E-Gazette after formality exam prior to registration. Application may be published immediately after filing provided description/claims/drawings comply with Regulations, filing and other fees fully paid, priority documents submitted if claimed, and other additional formal requirements complied with.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant actions on formality examination report (Rule 1412)
rubrics_metrics.description: Within two (2) months from mailing date of the formality exam report, applicant may amend the application, voluntarily withdraw, or convert to an invention patent application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If amending, reply and re-examination provisions in Part 9 Rules 911-913 apply mutatis mutandis. Failure to respond within two months causes withdrawal; Notice of Withdrawn Application mailed. Revival provisions apply mutatis mutandis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final action consequences (Rule 1413)
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant fails to file a complete response to formality exam report, any subsequent formality exam report submitted shall be a final action which may be appealed to the Director as provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary withdrawal procedure and effect (Rule 1414)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant may voluntarily withdraw by filing verified declaration of withdrawal and payment of fee; must identify application and be signed by applicant or assignee. Voluntarily withdrawn application shall not be revived and will be deemed forfeited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of withdrawal and opposition process (Rule 1414.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Declaration of withdrawal and application published in E-Gazette within 15 days of filing for purposes of opposition, unless declaration filed prior to 1st publication (then not published). Within 15 days from publication, any person prejudiced may present a written Opposition with fee in form of sworn statement substantiated by evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office not consider submissions failing requirements and shall dismiss for lack of compliance. If no Opposition or Opposition dismissed and Director satisfied, withdrawal granted and application deemed withdrawn as of date of grant publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director decision on opposition and appeal rights (Rule 1414.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Director decides whether Opposition should be granted; voluntary withdrawal held in abeyance until Opposition resolved. If Director grants Opposition and refuses withdrawal, applicant may appeal to Director General pursuant to IP Code Section 7.1(b) and Regulations; no motion for reconsideration of Director's decision allowed. If Director denies Opposition and grants withdrawal, application deemed withdrawn as of decision date and published as such.

rubrics_metrics.name: Term of utility model registration (Rule 1415)
rubrics_metrics.description: Utility model registration expires, without possibility of renewal, at end of seventh year after filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for cancellation of utility model registration (Rule 1416)
rubrics_metrics.description: Registration shall be cancelled if: (a) does not qualify as utility model; (b) does not meet novelty or industrial applicability or is non-registrable; (c) description/claims do not comply with prescribed requirements; (d) necessary drawing not furnished; (e) owner is not maker or successor in title.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion patent application to utility model (Rule 1417)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before grant or refusal of a patent for an invention, applicant may convert to a utility model application upon full payment of prescribed fee and be accorded the patent application's filing date; conversion permitted only once.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Converted application processed as utility model upon receipt of notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion utility model to patent application (Rule 1418)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before grant or refusal of utility model registration, applicant may convert to a patent application upon full payment of prescribed fee and be accorded utility model filing date; conversion only once.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Converted application processed as invention patent application upon receipt of notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adverse information presentation after conversion of published patent to utility model (Rule 1419)
rubrics_metrics.description: After conversion of a published patent application to a utility model application, any person may present written adverse information concerning registrability within one (1) month from community notification of conversion; converted application subject to adverse information proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition against filing parallel applications (Rule 1420)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibition against filing of parallel applications as provided in Part 9 Rule 915 of Patent Regulations applies mutatis mutandis to utility models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of industrial design (Rule 1500)
rubrics_metrics.description: An industrial design is any composition of shape, lines, colors, or combination, or any three-dimensional form producing an aesthetic and ornamental effect that gives special appearance and can serve as pattern for an industrial product or handicraft; includes appearance features like lines, contours, colors, shape, texture and/or materials and/or ornamentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Industrial product includes industrial items, handicraft items, parts intended for assembly, packaging, get-up, graphic symbols, typographic typefaces; excludes computer programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-registrable industrial designs (Rule 1501)
rubrics_metrics.description: Designs not registrable: (a) dictated essentially by technical/functional considerations to obtain technical result; (b) mere schemes of surface ornamentations existing separately from product/handicraft; (c) designs contrary to public order, health, or morals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requisite for registrability – novelty/originality (Rule 1502)
rubrics_metrics.description: To be registrable an industrial design must be new or original.

rubrics_metrics.name: Degree of novelty required and non-prejudicial disclosure period for designs (Rule 1503)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard of novelty per IP Code Sections 23 and 25 applies; period of non-prejudicial disclosure is six (6) months for designs (instead of 12 months). An industrial design not considered new if substantially similar to prior designs such that resemblance could be mistaken by an ordinary observer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial design application channels and required contents (Rule 1504)
rubrics_metrics.description: Application in writing in Filipino or English filed via IPOPHL electronic filing system, electronic format/internet, or IPSOs and addressed to the Director. Application shall contain: (a) request with indication that industrial design registration is sought, name/address and origin of right if applicant not designer, and indication of article kind; (b) description including title, applicant name, brief description of drawings, statement of characteristic features if any, and claim; (c) drawings of different views showing complete appearance with applicant signature; (d) payment of required fees at filing; (e) appointment of agent if applicant not a Philippine resident.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office may accept photographs or other adequate graphic representation if they comply with drawing requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment of fees for industrial design application (Rule 1505)
rubrics_metrics.description: Application subject to full payment of filing fee and publication fee upon filing. Applications claiming priority at filing must pay priority claim fee with filing and publication fee; priority claims within two (2) months subject to priority claim fee upon filing such claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of non-payment of fees for industrial designs (Rule 1505.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to pay all required fees in full upon filing means application not bona fide and deemed failed. Failed applications may be retrieved by formal written request within four (4) months from mailing date of notice of failed application; not retrieved are expunged; failed due to non-payment not published and may be filed anew.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special form of description for industrial design (Rule 1506)
rubrics_metrics.description: Description shall include: (a) title of design; (b) name of applicant (full name if natural person); (c) detailed description of different views/figures of formal drawings; (d) statement of characteristic features if any; (e) claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arranged in specified order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title requirements for industrial design (Rule 1506.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Title must technically designate the particular article embodying the design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brief description of drawing views (Rule 1506.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every view of the drawing should be briefly described (perspective, front, side, top, bottom, back) and given corresponding figure numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristic feature statement for designs (Rule 1506.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Statement describing particular novel and ornamental features of the claimed design which are considered dominant, if required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim form and limit for industrial designs (Rule 1506.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim shall be in formal terms of the ornamental design for the article, using phrases like '(specifying name) substantially as shown and described' or '(specifying name) substantially as shown'. More than one claim is neither required nor permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation requirements for industrial designs (Rule 1507)
rubrics_metrics.description: Representation shall consist of graphic or photographic reproduction, black & white or color. Representation must be clear and number of views must constitute a complete disclosure of appearance. Appropriate surface shading used to show character/contour; shading shall not be used to exemplify that a surface is colored.
